'''Nataša Jonoska''' ([[Macedonian language|Macedonian]]: Наташа Јоноска, {{IPA|mk|na'taʃa jɔ'noska|pron}}; born 1961,<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2002010775.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2018-12-10.</ref> also spelled '''Natasha Jonoska''') is a Macedonian [[mathematician]] and professor at the [[University of South Florida]] known for her work in [[DNA computing]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.usf.edu/faculty/njonoska/|title=Nataša Jonoska|website=USF Department of Mathematics & Statistics|access-date=2017-03-02|archive-date=2017-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303125026/http://www.math.usf.edu/faculty/njonoska/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her research is about how biology performs computation, "in particular using formal models such as cellular or other finite types of automata, formal language theory symbolic dynamics, and topological graph theory to describe molecular computation".<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783642401923#aboutAuthors|title=Discrete and Topological Models in Molecular Biology|first=Nataša|last=Jonoska|publisher=Springer|language=en}}</ref>

She received her [[bachelor's degree]] in mathematics  and computer science from [[Ss. Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje]] in [[Yugoslavia]] (now [[North Macedonia]]) in 1984.  She earned her PhD in mathematics from the [[Binghamton University|State University of New York at Binghamton]] in 1993 with the dissertation "Synchronizing Representations of [[Sofic system|Sofic Systems]]".<ref name=":0" />  Her dissertation advisor was [[Tom Head]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.binghamton.edu/gradnews/Newsletter.html|title=Mathematical Sciences Graduate Newsletter|date=2016-06-30|website=Binghamton University|access-date=2017-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307205854/http://www.math.binghamton.edu/gradnews/Newsletter.html|archive-date=2017-03-07|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2007, she won the [[International Society for Nanoscale Science, Computation, and Engineering#Tulip Award in DNA Computing|Rosenberg Tulip Award in DNA Computing]] for her work in applications of [[Automata theory]] and [[graph theory]] to [[DNA nanotechnology]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://isnsce.org/awards/the-rosenberg-tulip-award-in-dna-computing/|title=The Rosenberg Tulip Award in DNA Computing|date=2015-12-23|work=ISNSCE|access-date=2017-03-02|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303124610/https://isnsce.org/awards/the-rosenberg-tulip-award-in-dna-computing/|archive-date=2017-03-03|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She was elected a [[AAAS Fellow]] in 2014<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/jonoska-natasha|title=Jonoska, Natasha|date=2016-08-01|work=American Association for the Advancement of Science|access-date=2017-03-07|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307211213/https://www.aaas.org/fellow/jonoska-natasha|archive-date=2017-03-07|url-status=dead}}</ref> for advancements in understanding information processing in [[molecular self-assembly]].<ref name=":1" />  She is a board member for many journals including [[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|''Theoretical Computer Science'']],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/theoretical-computer-science/editorial-board|title=Theoretical Computer Science Editorial Board|access-date=March 2, 2017}}</ref> the ''[[International Journal of Foundations of Computer Science]]'', ''Computability'', and [[Natural Computing (journal)|''Natural Computing'']].<ref name=":0" /> In 2022 she was awarded a [[Simons Foundation|Simons]] Fellowship.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-18 |title=2022 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2022/02/18/2022-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/ |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=Simons Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Select publications==
* J. Chen, N. Jonoska, G. Rozenberg, (eds). ''Nanotechnology: Science and Computing'', Springer- Verlag 2006.
* N. Jonoska, Gh. Paun, G. Rozenberg, (eds.). ''Aspects of Molecular Computing LNCS 2950'', Springer-Verlag 2004.
* N. Jonoska, N.C. Seeman, (eds.). ''DNA Computing, Revised papers from the 7th International Meeting on DNA-Based Computers'', LNCS 2340, Springer-Verlag 2002.
